title: The Exile of El Cid
description: 1081-1094. Banished from Castile by King Alfonso VI, Rodrigo Diaz de Vivar must survive as a mercenary captain: serve the Muslim king of Zaragoza against his rivals, win battles that restore his reputation, and finally conquer Valencia in his own name. The player's small retinue grows through victories; losing El Cid himself means defeat.

anachronisms_found: SALADIN placed as the enemy hero: Salah ad-Din (1138-1193) was a Kurdish sultan of Egypt and Syria who was born some 40 years after El Cid's death and never set foot in Iberia. The engine offers plenty of anonymous Saracen alternatives (the KING unit already present, or a generic Castle-unit commander), so this was avoidable.

The enemy roster (CAMEL_RIDER x4, Saracen-style CASTLE/TENT_D/PAVILION_C, Saladin) directly contradicts the dialogue, which names the first opponent as a Christian 'rival Count' - the historical rivals of the Zaragoza campaign were Sancho Ramirez of Aragon and Berenguer Ramon II of Barcelona, who would field knights and crossbowmen, not desert cavalry.

MONASTERY on the Muslim player's side represents a mosque only by default; less objectionable given engine limits, but combined with the enemy KING it muddles the taifa of Valencia into a generic 'Saracen' polity.

TREE_PALM_FOREST x12 and SHORE_FISH as the dominant landscape for a campaign fought largely on the arid Aragonese/Levantine frontier reads as generic desert-Orient rather than the Ebro and Turia valleys.

Al-Mu'tamin of Zaragoza, El Cid's actual employer and named in the briefing text, is not placed at all - there is no allied third player, so the defining 'mercenary in Muslim service' relationship exists only as narration.
